title: Only 7% Can Name All These Obsolete Items
summary: Floppy disks, rotary phones, Walkmans and other everyday relics test how well you remember life before smartphones.

landing.intro: From floppy disks and rotary phones to Walkmans and washboards, see how many things from the past you still remember.

about.body:
This quick worldwide-English picture quiz revisits ten objects that were once part of everyday life. The challenge moves through communication, physical media, household work, writing technology and personal entertainment without relying on specialist historical knowledge.

The photographs are used with permission, and the questions retain the source quiz’s familiar visual-recognition style. Look closely at each object’s controls, shape and materials before choosing from the four possible names.

Your final percentage reflects this entertainment challenge only. Some objects remain in occasional, collectible or specialist use, so “obsolete” describes their disappearance from ordinary daily life rather than claiming that every example has vanished completely.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Inspect each photograph closely and identify the obsolete item shown.
Choose one of four answers. Correctness stays hidden until the final result.
Finish all ten pictures to reveal your Obsolete Objects Score and review every missed answer.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. Product names belong to their respective owners, and this quiz is not a formal history assessment.

profiles.title: The Retro Time Traveller
profiles.copy: You recognised the technology and everyday rituals of the pre-smartphone world almost instantly. Very little in this retro collection could catch you out.

profiles.title: The Obsolete Objects Expert
profiles.copy: You remembered an impressive range of forgotten devices and how people actually used them. Only one or two fading details escaped you.

profiles.title: The Analogue-Era Natural
profiles.copy: Most of these objects still felt familiar, even when their purpose required a second look. Your everyday technology memory is in excellent shape.

profiles.title: The Nostalgia Detective
profiles.copy: You decoded many of the visual clues while a few forgotten routines stayed mysterious. The answer review will reconnect the missing details.

profiles.title: The Retro Explorer
profiles.copy: Half of the collection brought back a clear memory and half felt like technology from another world. That is a solid result for a fast nostalgia challenge.

profiles.title: The Digital-Age Visitor
profiles.copy: Several obsolete objects proved genuinely unfamiliar, but every missed answer reveals a wonderfully strange piece of everyday history.

details.analysisTitle: How to read your retro score
details.analysisCopy: This ten-picture result combines communication devices, physical media, household tools, writing technology and personal entertainment. Each correct answer moves the headline percentage by ten points.
details.roadmapIntro: Your score is the first signal. Continue through the report to see which parts of everyday retro life felt most familiar and review every missed item.
details.positionCopy: The entertainment challenge target is eight correct answers out of ten. Your marker shows how close this attempt came.
details.measuredIntro: The ten selected photographs span five broad parts of pre-smartphone and pre-digital daily life.

measuredAreas.title: Communication and media
measuredAreas.copy: Recognising rotary telephones, pagers, portable cassette players and VHS tapes.

measuredAreas.title: Work and storage
measuredAreas.copy: Identifying typewriters and floppy disks from an era of physical writing and removable data.

measuredAreas.title: Household history
measuredAreas.copy: Remembering washboards, carpet beaters and bed warmers that performed familiar jobs without modern appliances.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to identify obsolete objects
details.tipsIntro: Use these clues if you attempt the picture challenge again.

tips.title: Look for physical controls
tips.copy: Rotary dials, tape doors, keys and hand-operated surfaces often reveal the object’s era and purpose.

tips.title: Notice what replaced it
tips.copy: Thinking about the modern phone, app or digital service that performs the same job can lead you back to the older object.

tips.title: Notice the materials
tips.copy: Corrugated metal, rattan, brass and thick moulded plastic can separate household tools from old entertainment technology.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?
questions.explanation: This is a floppy disk, the removable magnetic storage format widely used to save and transfer computer files in the 1980s and 1990s.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A black and brass telephone with a circular numbered dial

questions.explanation: This is a rotary phone. Users placed a finger in the numbered wheel, turned it to the stop and released it for every digit.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A red stereoscopic viewer with two black eyepieces

questions.explanation: This is a View-Master. A round reel of paired images was inserted into the viewer to create a stereoscopic 3D effect.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A black mechanical writing machine with rows of round keys

questions.explanation: This is a typewriter. Pressing a key moved a metal type element against an inked ribbon to print a character on paper.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A wood-framed board with a corrugated metal washing surface

questions.explanation: This is a washboard. Clothes were scrubbed by hand against its corrugated surface before automatic washing machines became common.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A black portable cassette player with lightweight headphones

questions.explanation: This is a Sony Walkman, the portable cassette player launched in 1979 that made private music listening possible on the move.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: Several rectangular video cassettes stacked on a video recorder

questions.explanation: This is a VHS tape, the magnetic video format that dominated home movie viewing before DVDs became widespread.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: Two woven rattan tools with long handles and looped heads

questions.explanation: This is a carpet beater. Rugs were hung outdoors and struck with the tool to knock loose dust out of the fibres.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A small black belt-worn electronic device with a narrow numeric display

questions.explanation: This is a pager, also known as a beeper. It received short numeric or alphanumeric messages over a radio network.

questions.question: What is the name of this old item?

image.alt: A perforated brass pan with a long dark handle

questions.explanation: This is a bed warmer. Hot coals were placed inside the long-handled metal pan, which was moved beneath the bedclothes to warm the mattress.
